question: A cyclist on the flat doubles speed from 20 to 40 km/h. By what factor does the power needed against air drag rise?
answer: About 8 times. Drag force grows with the square of speed, and power is force times speed, so it grows with the cube. At 20 km/h a typical rider spends roughly 35 W on the air; at 40 km/h roughly 290 W, more than most riders can hold for an hour.
move: Ask which power of the number the cost actually follows.
trap: Assuming power rises in step with speed.
reference: Wilson, Bicycling Science, 3rd ed., MIT Press, 2004
